Class GameController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.gui.GameController
public class GameController extends Object
JavaFX controller for the main in-game screen (gameBoard.fxml).

GameController is the single point of contact between the network layer and the game UI. It receives update callbacks from ViewGUI (which is itself notified by the VirtualModel) and translates them into visual changes: card rows, tile board, totem positions, player statistics, flag icons, event banners, and era curtain animations.

All public and private methods that touch JavaFX nodes are guarded by assertFxThread(), which throws IllegalStateException if called from outside the FX Application Thread.

Lifecycle

  1. initialize() — called by the FXMLLoader; wires button handlers and installs stat-icon tooltips.
  2. refreshBoard() — called by ViewGUI on every model update; delegates to initStructure() on the first call and to syncState() on every subsequent call.

Event-banner and era-animation sequencing

The server may send two consecutive EventMessages in the same round (round events followed by end-game events). To prevent the second banner from being lost, incoming events are enqueued in pendingEventBanners while a banner is already on screen. Era curtain animations are similarly deferred in pendingEraAnimations and played once all event banners have been dismissed.

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Called automatically by the FXMLLoader after all @FXML fields have been injected.

      Wires the skip-button handler, enables hover cursor on the menu icon, and installs custom tooltips on all stat icons.

    • onMenuBtnClick

      private void onMenuBtnClick(javafx.scene.input.MouseEvent event)
      FXML handler invoked when the player clicks the menuBtn image.

      Convenience overload that delegates to onMenuBtnClick(MouseEvent, Node) with null as the fallback node, so that any confirmation dialog's "Back" button returns to the pause menu itself rather than to a previous overlay.

      Parameters:
      event - the mouse-click event fired by the FXML binding

    • onMenuBtnClick

      private void onMenuBtnClick(javafx.scene.input.MouseEvent event, javafx.scene.Node fallback)
      Opens the in-game pause menu overlay.

      The menu exposes three actions: close the application entirely, abandon the current match and return to the main menu (triggers ClientToServerActions.quit()), or dismiss the menu. If fallback is non-null it is restored as the overlay content when the user navigates back from a confirmation dialog.

      Parameters:
      event - the mouse event that triggered the call, or null when invoked programmatically
      fallback - optional node to restore when the user clicks "back" inside the confirm dialog; pass null to close the overlay entirely

    • showConfirm

      private void showConfirm(String title, String caption, Runnable onConfirm)
      Shows a two-button confirmation dialog (Confirm / Back) inside the global overlay. Clicking Confirm hides the overlay and runs onConfirm; clicking Back navigates to fallback (or to the pause menu if fallback is null).
      Parameters:
      title - bold headline text shown at the top of the dialog
      caption - secondary descriptive text shown below the headline
      onConfirm - action executed when the user confirms

    • showConfirm

      private void showConfirm(String title, String caption, Runnable onConfirm, javafx.scene.Node fallback)
      Shows a two-button confirmation dialog (Confirm / Back) inside the global overlay. Clicking Confirm hides the overlay and runs onConfirm; clicking Back restores fallback as the overlay content, or re-opens the pause menu if fallback is null.
      Parameters:
      title - bold headline text shown at the top of the dialog
      caption - secondary descriptive text shown below the headline
      onConfirm - action executed when the user confirms
      fallback - node to restore on "Back", or null to reopen the menu

    • createTooltip

      private void createTooltip(javafx.scene.image.ImageView target, String title, String desc)
      Installs a custom styled tooltip on the given ImageView.

      The tooltip is composed of a bold title and a wrapping description text, styled via the card-tooltip CSS class. It is installed only once per node; repeated calls for the same target are silently ignored.

      Parameters:
      target - the node on which the tooltip is installed
      title - short label displayed in bold at the top
      desc - longer description shown below the title

    • refreshBoard

      public void refreshBoard()
      Refreshes the board to reflect the current state of the VirtualModel.

      On the first invocation (initialized is false) the full scene structure is built by initStructure(). On every subsequent call only the dynamic state (card rows, totem positions, stats, phase labels) is re-synchronized via syncState().

      If the current turn number differs from lastTurn, a round-boundary animation is triggered via onEndRound().

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • insertCard

      public void insertCard(int cardId)
      Moves the card identified by cardId from the draw rows into the local player's village column for its type.

      The card is explicitly removed from all four draw-row HBoxes before being appended to the appropriate VBox column. If no column exists yet for the card's type, a new one is created and added to myVillage. Duplicate insertions are prevented by checking whether a column already holds the card.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      cardId - the unique identifier of the card to insert; must be present in cardMap

    • showNotification

      private void showNotification(String message, String colorHex)
      Displays a temporary notification message at the top of the notificationBox.

      The message fades out after 2.5 seconds and is then removed from the scene graph. Notifications are stacked in reverse insertion order (newest on top).

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      message - the text to display
      colorHex - CSS hex color string applied to the message text (e.g. "#3498db")

    • onChangeAge

      public void onChangeAge(int age)
      Handles an era-change notification from the server.

      Updates the era label and the deck display. If an event banner is currently on screen (or pending banners are queued), the curtain animation is deferred in pendingEraAnimations and will play once all banners have been dismissed; otherwise it is shown immediately via showEraCurtainAnimation(int).

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      age - the new era number (1-based)

    • showEraCurtainAnimation

      private void showEraCurtainAnimation(int age)
      Plays the era-change curtain animation.

      Two dark panels slide in from the top and bottom of the screen, meet in the center, reveal an era title (e.g. "ERA II") for roughly 1.8 seconds, then slide back out. The animation is built entirely from JavaFX TranslateTransitions and FadeTransitions assembled in a SequentialTransition.

      An AnimationTimer is used to wait two rendering frames before reading the panel heights, ensuring that layout has been performed and the measurements are accurate.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      age - the era number to display, converted to a Roman numeral by toRoman(int)

    • toRoman

      private String toRoman(int n)
      Converts a small positive integer to its Roman-numeral string.
      Parameters:
      n - the number to convert (expected values: 1, 2, 3)
      Returns:
      the Roman-numeral string, or an empty string for unrecognized values

      public void onEvent(EventDTO events, List<PlayerStatsDTO> statsBefore)
      Displays the event banner for the given EventDTO.

    • showEventBanner

      Builds and displays the slide-in banner for a single EventDTO.

      The banner contains the event card images, a per-player stat-delta summary, and an auto-dismissing progress bar. It slides in from the left and is automatically hidden after 8 seconds via hideBanner().

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:

      statsBefore - pre-event stats used to compute per-player deltas

      Transitions to the end-game leaderboard screen.

      Loads leaderboardBoard.fxml, passes the final ranking data to LeaderboardController, and replaces the current scene with the leaderboard in full-screen mode.

    • showLeaderboard

      public void showLeaderboard(Map<PlayerDTO, Integer> ranks)
      Populates and reveals the global leaderboard table inside the LeaderboardController that was loaded during onGameEnding(List, int, int).

      Called by ViewGUI.showLeaderboard(Map) on the FX Application Thread after the server responds to a global-ranking request. The map is forwarded to the leaderboard controller, which sorts the entries and renders them in the persistent-ranking table view.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread; enforced by assertFxThread().

      Parameters:

    • initStructure

      private void initStructure()
      Performs the one-time structural setup of the scene: board tiles, queue tile, deck widget, totem pawns, card rows, player stats, and opponent village overlays.

      This method is intentionally separated from syncState() so that the fixed scene structure is built only once, even when refreshBoard() is called repeatedly.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • syncState

      private void syncState()
      Synchronizes all dynamic GUI elements with the current state of the VirtualModel.

      Covers: totem positions, card rows, village columns, player stats, phase / turn / age labels, drawable highlights, and the deck widget. Called on every refreshBoard() invocation, including after a reconnection.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • updateTotemPositions

      private void updateTotemPositions()
      Re-reads totem positions from the virtual model and places every totem on either the queue tile or the appropriate board tile.

      Clears all existing pawn placements before re-populating, so the result always reflects the authoritative server state.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • initVillagePanel

      private void initVillagePanel()
      Creates and attaches the VillagePanel floating panel to the scene root, then redirects myVillage to the panel's inner HBox.

      The panel is inserted immediately below globalOverlay in the z-order so that it appears behind modal overlays. Idempotent: does nothing if the panel has already been created.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • initStatsPanel

      private void initStatsPanel()
      Creates and attaches the StatsPanel floating panel to the scene root, then redirects opponents to the panel's inner VBox.

      The panel is inserted immediately below globalOverlay in the z-order and aligned to the right edge of the screen. Idempotent: does nothing if the panel has already been created.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • initOpponentOverlays

      private void initOpponentOverlays(List<PlayerDTO> players)
      Builds a GameController.VillageOverlay for each opponent player and stores it in opponentOverlays.

      Each overlay contains one VBox column per CardTypeEnum; columns are hidden until populated. The overlay is shown when the local player clicks the "+" button next to an opponent's name.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

      Parameters:
      players - the full player list; the local player is skipped

    • updateVillages

      private void updateVillages()
      Rebuilds all village columns from the current virtual-model snapshot.

      For the local player, cards are inserted into myVillage via insertCard(int). For opponents, cards are inserted into the corresponding GameController.VillageOverlay. Duplicate card IDs within the same player are filtered out using a local Set.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread (indirectly via syncState()).

    • refreshDrawableHighlight

      private void refreshDrawableHighlight()
      Recomputes and applies highlight states to all cards and tiles.

      Highlights are shown only when it is the local player's turn:

      • During DRAW_PHASE / OPTIONAL_DRAW_PHASE: cards that the player can afford and are in the correct row are highlighted; arrow indicators on the player's tile show remaining up/down draw counts.
      • During SETUP_PHASE: unoccupied tiles are highlighted as valid placement targets.

      The skip button is shown only when the current draw action is optional (as indicated by ActionsDTO.isSkippable()).

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • isDrawable

      private boolean isDrawable(CardDTO c)
      Returns true if the local player can draw the given card.

      Buildings are drawable only when the player has enough food to cover their cost after applying the build discount. Character cards are always drawable; event cards (Feast, Hunt, Ritual, StonePainting) are never directly drawable by the player.

      Parameters:
      c - the card DTO to evaluate
      Returns:
      true if the card can currently be drawn by the local player

    • animateDeal

      private void animateDeal(List<CardGUI> cards)
      Plays a staggered deal animation for a list of cards: each card fades in showing its back, then flips to reveal its front via paired ScaleTransitions. Cards are animated with a base delay of 80 ms × index to produce a cascading effect.
      Parameters:
      cards - the cards to animate, in display order

    • dealSingleCard

      private void dealSingleCard(CardGUI card)
      Animates a single card's deal sequence: fade in → scale to zero (showing back) → swap to front image → scale back to full size.
      Parameters:
      card - the card to animate
